The store of works keyed by a canonical id — a braincrawl-minted UUID, opaque and provider-neutral. Holds each work's artifacts: abstracts, fulltexts, and derived projections.

A work's single, braincrawl-minted identity — a UUID. Every external identifier (DOI, ISBN, OpenAlex id, Semantic Scholar id) maps to exactly one canonical id.
The primary edge between catalog entries: one work citing another. Forward traversal is `cited-by`, backward is `refs`.
Scholarly metadata provider — the broadest source: entity get, search, filter, autocomplete, and citations in both directions.

The PWA chat client. A thin client, never a replica: it fetches the doc and page chunks it needs, edits docs via the normalizing PUT, and pushes what it gathers from OpenAlex into the Cloudflare store. Local state is only the conversation (localStorage) and per-session caches.
Citation-data provider — deposited reference lists only (`refs`); no search.
One `<slug>.l3.md`: frontmatter + `##` nodes with `^r-` anchors, property and link lines. Points at works by canonical id.
The provider contract: `GET /works/{id}` and `GET /works?search=` over HTTPS, JSON. Polite pool via `mailto`; rate-limited. This is the shape both agents gather against.

The CLI's HTTP client for the store API. Every store-facing command goes through it; the configured base URL decides whether it talks to the Local or the Cloudflare store.

The one HTTP surface both store implementations serve, held identical by the shared conformance suite (`crates/conformance`). Bearer-token auth on the worker.

```
PUT  /works                          upsert works + aliases → canonical ids
PUT  /edges                          upsert citation edges
POST /works/have                     presence check by alias
POST /graph/neighborhood             bounded BFS from seed ids
GET  /stats                          aggregate counts
GET|PUT /works/{id}/content/{role}   artifact bytes by role
POST /jobs                           enqueue background fetch
GET  /health                         liveness probe (unauthenticated)
```

L2 seam, the richest trait — the queryable graph facts. All methods async, returning `Result<_, DomainError>`.

```rust
// identity
get_alias(alias) -> Option<CanonicalId>
get_or_create_alias(alias, candidate) -> CanonicalId  // UNIQUE(ns,value); returns the winner
resolve_live(id) -> CanonicalId   // follow merged_into chain, path-compressed
merge(survivor, loser)            // repoint everything, tombstone the loser
// metadata (Option A: provider assertions verbatim, merged at read time)
create_node(id, kind, created_at)
upsert_node_assertion(id, source, attrs, fetched_at)
read_node(id) -> Option<(kind, [(source, attrs, fetched_at)], [alias])>
// citation graph
put_edge(src, dst, relation, source, attrs?, fetched_at)
read_edges(id, dir, cursor?, limit) -> ([EdgeView], next_cursor?)
// queries
present_aliases([alias]) -> [alias]   // backs 'have'
stats() -> GraphStats
```

The worker's L3 surface: PUT validates the node grammar, normalizes, assigns missing `^r-` anchors, stamps `updated:`; GET serves raw markdown; `/api/l3/graph` serves the parsed graph with an ETag.

The SQLite/D1 tables behind the store traits. works, authors, venues, concepts, topics are all `node`, differing by `kind`; provider records are stored verbatim as JSON assertions and merged at read time (per-field provenance, doc02.01.01).

```sql
-- L2: identity + metadata + citation graph (0002)
node(canonical_id PK, kind, created_at, merged_into)
  -- no assertions yet = stub; merged_into set = tombstone, never deleted
alias(scheme, value, canonical_id)   PK (scheme, value)
  -- the convergence guarantee: an external id can never fork
node_assertion(canonical_id, source, attrs JSON, fetched_at)   PK (id, source)
edge(src_id, dst_id, relation)          PK (src, dst, relation)
edge_assertion(src_id, dst_id, relation, source, attrs JSON, fetched_at)

-- L1: artifact descriptors (0001; 0004 renamed payloads→artifacts, kind→role)
artifacts(canonical_id, role, version, r2_key, content_hash, byte_size,
          mime, source, source_url, fetched_at, is_current)
  PK (canonical_id, role, version);  r2_key = {id}/{role}/v{version}

-- jobs (0003)
fetch_jobs(id PK, kind, target_id, params JSON, state, attempts,
           run_after, last_error, created_at, updated_at)
  UNIQUE (kind, target_id) WHERE state IN ('pending','running')
```

The platform-agnostic use-case layer (`crates/core/src/usecases.rs`, doc02.01.03) — one struct assembled from seven seams; each deployment is this struct with different parts.

```rust
Store<M, B, P, R, C, Clk, Id>
  M:   MetadataStore     B: BlobStore      P: ArtifactStore
  R:   IdResolver        C: Coordinator    // with_lock(key) -> LockGuard
  Clk: Clock             Id: IdGen
```

Owns the domain policy no trait signature shows:

```
lock key    highest-priority alias scheme:
            doi > pmid > pmcid > openalex > semantic_scholar > arxiv
read merge  newest fetched_at wins per field; tie-break = lexicographically
            smallest source; provenance map records each winner
new work    unknown alias -> mint GUID (IdGen), remember (IdResolver)
```

Per-work single-writer seam — only `usecases::Store` takes it, wrapping every write. Async, `Result<_, DomainError>`.

```rust
with_lock(key) -> LockGuard   // dropping the guard releases
```

Lock key = the work's highest-priority alias (policy owned by `usecases::Store`).

impls: `LocalCoordinator` (native, in-process) · `DoCoordinator` (worker, Durable Object)

Resolved once at startup; precedence env > `~/.config/braincrawl/config.toml` > default. `server_url` is the switch deciding which store every command talks to.

```toml
server_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8787"  # the store switch
openalex_api_key = "…"               # optional
semanticscholar_api_key = "…"        # optional
auth_token = "…"                     # bearer token for the worker store
unpaywall_email = "…"                # fetch-content URL resolution
crossref_mailto = "…"                # crossref polite pool
l3_repo = "~/…/braincrawl-l3"        # L3 root; default ~/.local/share/braincrawl/l3
```

Every field is env-overridable (`BRAINCRAWL_*`).

**Shared input shape.** `main.rs` locally converts the provider-specific `OpenalexCmd` into this provider-neutral enum. It is a data transformation, not a trait call and not an HTTP request.

```rust
#[serde(tag = "verb")]
enum ProviderCmd {
  Get { id }, Search { entity: Option<String>, query },
  Find { entity, filters }, Autocomplete { entity, q },
  CitedBy { id }, Refs { id },
}
```

It is the input shape accepted by `Provider::dispatch`.

Input to Clap. This is process input, not yet a Rust command value.

fn run_provider(
  p: &dyn Provider,
  cmd: ProviderCmd,
  store: &StoreClient,
  opts: &OutputOpts,
) -> Result<()>

Calls p.dispatch; then renders its Envelope and, unless --skip-push, pushes its Emission.

list(entity, ListParams) -> Result<ListPage>

Builds the query URL, then reqwest::blocking::Client sends GET to api.openalex.org. Retries HTTP 429 and 5xx responses (up to 3 retries).

This is the OpenAlex network-effect boundary.

Result<(Envelope, Emission), ProviderError>

Envelope: user-facing query metadata + display results.
Emission: store-ready WorkRecord[] + EdgeInput[].

The provider produces both from the same fetched OpenAlex records; the result returns to run_provider.
**Output effect.** `render(&envelope, opts)` writes the display Envelope to stdout, or `--emission` writes the store-ready Emission instead.
The complete OpenAlex provider: an external scholarly service, its HTTP contract, and Braincrawl's adapter that carries the shared provider protocol across that boundary.

The shared Rust vocabulary between the CLI and provider implementations: one command shape, one dispatch contract, and one paired result shape.

Each provider-specific adapter enters and leaves through this protocol.

The Crossref provider path: it backfills reference lists through Crossref's deposited-reference HTTP surface.

`CrossrefProvider` implements `Provider` and flows through `run_provider` like the other adapters. Because Crossref keys by DOI, `resolve_doi` converts the work id to a DOI before dispatch.
The keyless arXiv provider: its preprint API and Braincrawl adapter. It uses the shared `ProviderCmd` / `Provider` protocol, but supports only `get` and `search`.
Public arXiv preprint API. Braincrawl queries it for individual records and Atom-feed search results; no API key is configured.

get(id) / search(query) -> Result<String>

Builds a public `export.arxiv.org/api/query` request and sends it with blocking reqwest. It returns raw Atom XML, which `arxiv::parse` lowers. This is arXiv's network-effect boundary.

`alias.rs` — the CLI's shared id-alias vocabulary.

- `parse(&str) -> Option<Alias>` recognizes an id's scheme (`doi:`, `openalex:`, a DOI URL, a bare `10./…` DOI).
- `alias_of(&Value, ns)` pulls one scheme out of a store work.

Consumers: `resolve_doi` and fetch-content's Unpaywall lookup.

DOI-keyed providers (Crossref, OpenCitations) key by DOI, not the catalog work id. `resolve_doi` runs before dispatch:

- `alias::parse` accepts an id already in DOI form — no store read.
- otherwise `store.get_work` then `alias::alias_of(work, "doi")`.

The bare DOI becomes `ProviderCmd::Refs { id }`.

`impl Provider for CrossrefProvider`. Supports `ProviderCmd::Refs` only; every other verb returns `ProviderError::UnsupportedVerb`. `dispatch` receives an id already resolved to a DOI and returns `(Envelope, Emission)` — the emission carries `EdgeInput` citation edges, no work records.

The CLI command-execution path: from the raw process argument vector, through Clap parsing and command lowering, to `run_provider` dispatch and rendered output. DOI-keyed providers resolve the work id to a DOI (`resolve_doi` → `alias`) before dispatch.

The `ProviderCmd` and `Provider` trait stages of this same path live in the Providers container.

The native binary `apps/server` — an axum HTTP server over a stable SQLite file + on-disk blob dir under `~/.local/share/braincrawl`, run as the `braincrawl-server` systemd user service on `127.0.0.1:8787`.

It instantiates `usecases::Store` with the native backends:

```rust
pub type LocalStore = Store<
  SqliteStore, FsBlobStore, SqliteStore,
  MemResolver, LocalCoordinator,
  SystemClock, UuidGen>;   // server/lib.rs:92
```

Same policy struct as the worker; only the seven parts differ.

**Serves the Store HTTP contract.** `Router::new().route("/works/*path", …)` — one `.route` per path, health unauthenticated, the rest behind an optional bearer layer (disabled on localhost).

server/lib.rs:697
Satisfies both `MetadataStore` (L2) and `ArtifactStore` (L1) over one SQLite file — the two type params `M` and `P` are the same type here.
`BlobStore` over a directory of files under the blob root.
`IdResolver` alias→canonical cache, in-process memory.
`Coordinator` single-writer lock, in-process.
`Clock` from the OS wall clock.
`IdGen` minting UUIDv4 canonical ids.

The Cloudflare Worker `apps/worker` — a Durable-Object `fetch` handler backed by D1 (SQL), R2 (blobs), and KV (resolver cache).

It instantiates the same `usecases::Store` with the WASM/Cloudflare backends:

```rust
type WorkerStore = Store<
  D1Store, R2BlobStore, D1Store,
  KvResolver, DoCoordinator,
  WasmClock, WasmIdGen>;   // worker/lib.rs:78
```

**Serves the identical Store HTTP contract** — no axum. A `match method { … }` over `(method, path)` inside the Durable Object's `fetch`.

worker/lib.rs:666
Satisfies both `MetadataStore` (L2) and `ArtifactStore` (L1) over Cloudflare D1 — the same type fills `M` and `P`, as SqliteStore does natively.
`BlobStore` over a Cloudflare R2 bucket.
`IdResolver` alias→canonical cache, backed by Workers KV.
`Coordinator` single-writer lock routed through a `WorkDurableObject` keyed by lock key.
`Clock` from the Worker runtime clock.
`IdGen` minting canonical ids in the WASM runtime.

**`crates/conformance` — what keeps the two servers serving the *same* REST API.**

```rust
run_all(base_url, token) -> Result<(), String>  // lib.rs:5
```

One suite of API assertions, run against BOTH deployments: the native server in-process, and the worker under wrangler via `scripts/worker-conformance.sh`. If a route drifts on one side, this fails — so the Store HTTP contract is enforced, not merely documented.
